subject: Reserved capacity: pricing sensitivity & tactical approval checklist
messages:
From: Evelyn Marsh <evelyn@acme.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity question — pricing sensitivity and approvals

Hi David,

Thanks for taking a look at this. We're finalizing our Q4 product roadmap and are evaluating a reserved capacity commit with Redwood. Two quick asks: 1) how sensitive is the committed unit price to GPU market swings — specifically, what discount path do you offer if market spot drops 20% vs your committed rate? 2) what internal approvals do you need for a discount deeper than the standard schedule (we may ask for a one-time concession tied to a 24-month commit).

Sizing context: we expect ~6M tokens/month initially, spiking to 18M tokens/month in month 6. Preferred region: us-west. We'll need a predictable latency SLO (p95 < 200ms) and private tenancy for some models.

Can you share a quick sensitivity sketch and the approvals checklist so procurement can budget?

Appreciate it — Evelyn
Evelyn Marsh
Director, ML Platform
Acme AI

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Marsh <evelyn@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity question — pricing sensitivity and approvals

Evelyn — thanks for the context and the clear sizing. Attaching a short capacity_breakdown.xlsx (high-level) that maps token ranges to SKU bundles we recommend. High-level answers below, and I've looped Monica from deal ops for the approvals checklist.

Highlights:
- Baseline: committed per-token pricing is anchored to our standard reserved SKU table.
- Market pass-through: we offer a limited price-index clause for multi-year deals (applies only if GPU spot pricing deviates >25% sustained over 30 days).
- Tactical concession: we can offer an upfront credit or a transient discount for the first 3 months tied to ramp milestones; deeper list-price discounts (>15%) require finance sign-off and VP approval.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share three pricing scenarios (conservative / mid / aggressive) with explicit sensitivity lines to GPU cost moves.
2) Monica will circulate a one-page approvals checklist (who signs off at each discount tier).
3) If you’re comfortable, share your forecast cadence (monthly projection file) and we’ll size a phased activation plan that keeps latency SLOs intact while minimizing committed spend.

On the SLO/tenancy side we can guarantee p95 < 200ms on the dedicated pool with network isolation; we’ll attach the SLO appendix to the SOW.

-David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity question — approvals checklist draft

Forwarding my draft approvals checklist and a proposed SOW version (SOW_v3.pdf). Below is the internal ask + recommended approval routing.

Internal summary:
- Request: 24-month reserved commit for Acme AI; initial committed usage ~6M tokens/mo with phased activation to 18M tokens/mo by month 6.
- Discount ask: Acme is likely to request a 20% list discount capped at the reserved SKU level or an equivalent credit.
- Risk: GPU market could fall, which increases our margin exposure if the committed prices remain fixed.

Recommended routing / thresholds:
- up to 10% discount: AE + Sales Manager approval (no finance review)
- 10%–20%: AE + Sales Manager + Finance (Revenue Operations) sign-off
- >20%: AE + Sales Manager + Finance + VP Sales approval (exec exceptions group)

Mitigations to propose in the contract:
- phased activation (monthly ramps) so we only provision extra GPU pools as utilization hits thresholds
- credit/true-up mechanism if market spot price drops below an agreed floor for >60 days
- optional indexation clause with caps (trigger + floor)

Please weigh in on whether we should preemptively ask Acme to agree to a quarterly true-up; that reduces our upfront GPU exposure.

-Monica
Head of Deal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity question — approvals checklist draft

Thanks — ran the numbers vs three GPU-cost scenarios (stable / -20% spot / -40% spot). Key takeaways below (short):

Scenario math (high level):
- Stable: gross margin vs reserved list baseline is healthy (~42% on recommended SKU mix).
- -20% spot: realized margin tightens to ~28% if we are fully provisioned and no true-up; still tolerable for short periods but not sustainable for 24 months.
- -40% spot: margin becomes single digits; unacceptable without contractual true-up or index clause.

Recommendation (pricing instruments):
- Offer a 12% upfront customer discount + a 6% ramp credit that vests over first 6 months (effective ~18% first-year concession) — this is finance-friendly and tied to usage milestones.
- Add a market-index trigger: if GPU spot < floor (30% below baseline) for >60 days, contract enters a true-up negotiation (not automatic pass-through).
- Require a procurement signature that commits to monthly forecast cadence; if forecast misses by >25% for 2 consecutive months, we reserve right to re-evaluate provisioning and pricing.

Approvals required: finance sign-off recommended for the combined 18% effective concession. Anything above that should be routed to VP Sales for exec approval.

-Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Marsh <evelyn@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity question — pricing sensitivity and approvals

Evelyn — appreciate the patience while we pulled internal scenarios together. See the proposal summary below (short):

Proposal summary (Acme AI — 24-month reserved commit):
- Committed baseline: 6M tokens/mo for months 1–3, phased to 18M tokens/mo by month 6. Region: us-west. Dedicated tenancy.
- Commercial: 12% list discount up front + a 6% usage ramp credit (applies if monthly usage meets agreed ramp milestones) = ~18% effective concession in year 1.
- Protections for Redwood: market-index trigger and true-up clause (if GPU spot < 30% below baseline for >60 days, we open a true-up discussion).
- Approvals: finance has pre-cleared the 18% effective concession; anything >18% requires VP Sales approval.

Attachments & links: capacity_breakdown.xlsx (detailed SKU map), SOW_v3.pdf (SLO appendix included), DocuSign link for the SOW and order form: https://docusign.com/link/abcdef123456

If that looks reasonable, we can send a redline-friendly SOW and route a DocuSign packet to your procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the sensitivity table.

Best,
David
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Marsh <evelyn@acme.ai>

Thanks team — this is exactly the detail we needed. The blended 18% first-year concession aligns with our finance plan; the market-trigger clause is acceptable as long as the true-up process is clearly defined.

Procurement, please take the DocuSign link and SOW and start internal routing. I’ll schedule a 30-min review with David next week to confirm ramp milestones. Attaching our contract routing doc for your intake.

-Evelyn
Evelyn Marsh

Acme AI
